question: Why did the error rate go up on 05 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of checkout v8.10 to eu-west may have caused the error rate to increase in us-east.
why_chain: checkout v8.10 deployment to eu-west introduced a change that affected service catalog in us-east.
The change in checkout v8.10 deployment caused an error rate increase in service catalog in us-east.
The error rate increase in service catalog in us-east is reflected in the error rate metric.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of search v4.8 to us-east may have caused the error rate to increase in us-east.
why_chain: search v4.8 deployment to us-east introduced a change that affected service catalog in us-east.
The change in search v4.8 deployment caused an error rate increase in service catalog in us-east.
The error rate increase in service catalog in us-east is reflected in the error rate metric.

contributing_factors.description: The slow query on the auth endpoint in ap-south may have caused the error rate to increase in us-east.
why_chain: The slow query on the auth endpoint in ap-south may have caused a delay in processing requests.
This delay may have affected the service catalog in us-east, causing an error rate increase.
The error rate increase in service catalog in us-east is reflected in the error rate metric.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a sudden increase in request volume.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service catalog in us-east did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate was due to a sudden increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: The p95 latency for service catalog in us-east did not change significantly.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog in region us-east rose from 0.38% to 0.75% (+98%), with a change point at 2026-03-05T06:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog in region us-east: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.10).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (731 per 5 min before, 863 per 5 min after, +18%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (120 ms before, 121 ms after, +1%).
Deployed checkout v8.10 to eu-west (checkout, eu-west; 7 min before the change; record R008)
Deployed search v4.8 to us-east (routine release) (search, us-east; 265 min before the change; record R006)
auth: WARN slow query 1.2s on report endpoint (single occurrence) (auth, ap-south; 139 min before the change; record R007)

reasons: ✓ A change event (deploys) lines up in time (7 min before the change).
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records for the affected service/region
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Rollback the checkout v8.10 deployment to eu-west.
Monitor the performance of the search v4.8 deployment to us-east closely.
Investigate the slow query on the auth endpoint in ap-south further.
